slides.headline: 6 PROMPTS THAT WORK YOUR $3,200-A-MONTH NIGHT SHIFT FOR FREE
1) ANSWER EVERY CUSTOMER EMAIL OVERNIGHT
slides.body: A night-shift rep costs $3,200 a month to answer emails while you sleep. 'Here are my unread customer emails. Sort by urgency, draft a reply for each, flag any that need me personally'

slides.headline: 2) CATCH EVERY WRONG CHARGE BEFORE BREAKFAST
slides.body: An auditor charges $150 an hour to catch what slips through while you sleep. 'Here is my bank statement. Flag anything over $200 I didn't authorize and tell me if spending changed'

slides.headline: 3) PREP EVERY MEETING BEFORE YOUR ALARM
slides.body: Meeting prep costs managers 4 hours every week. This runs while they sleep. 'Here is my calendar for tomorrow. For each meeting: who is there, what they care about, three points I should raise'

slides.headline: 4) COLLECT YOUR UNPAID INVOICES AT DAWN
slides.body: Chasing payments eats 15 hours a month you could spend sleeping. 'Here are my outstanding invoices. Find every one past due and draft a firm but polite follow-up for each'

slides.headline: 5) SORT YOUR TEAM'S UPDATES BY MORNING
slides.body: A manager reads 100+ messages a day, most arriving overnight. 'Here are today's messages from my team. Five bullets: what got done, what is stuck, what needs my decision tomorrow'

slides.headline: 6) SCREEN YOUR NEXT HIRE BEFORE COFFEE
slides.body: Screening resumes takes 23 hours per role that you could sleep through. 'Here are 20 applications. Score each 1-10 on my criteria and show me only the top 3 with why each wins'

slides.headline: SAVE THIS FOR THE NIGHT YOU NEED IT
slides.body: You'll want these prompts when you're drowning at midnight. Save this post and paste them when the work piles up. Daily AI news and real skills at @yaffeai

caption:
Swipe for 6 prompts that keep your business running while you sleep. One for every part you hate doing by hand 🔥

Customer emails answered overnight, wrong charges caught before breakfast, every meeting prepped before your alarm, unpaid invoices chased at dawn, team updates sorted into five bullets by morning, and job applications ranked before your first coffee.

The people pulling ahead right now aren't working more hours. They paste six prompts before bed and wake up to a business that already moved without them.
